data.description:
# Goal

Make the 05:00 nightly proxy usage report publish the two capacity-signal
metrics — the `slots_stale` (stale-poll) rate and the `capacity_hint`
distribution including `saturated`-without-live-work — so every night can be
compared directly against the "< 5 % stale" and "saturated only with live
work" targets without a separate standalone tool run and hand cross-check.

## Problem statement

`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` derives `slots_stale` rate,
`capacity_hint` distribution and saturated-without-live-work counts for an
arbitrary window, but the canonical nightly report
(`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`, cron at 05:00) emits neither. The post-fix
night window (2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00) therefore had to be measured
with the standalone tool and reconciled against `report.md` by hand — only
`Local attempts` (206/206) and the restart timeline could be cross-checked, so
the capacity figures had no nightly counterpart. Every future night carries the
same gap, and the two AC1 re-measurements queued after it
(LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ) would each need another ad-hoc run.

## Users

- **Operator reading the 05:00 report** — "as the operator, I want tonight's
  `report.md` to show the stale-poll rate against its target, so I can judge
  the polling-path health without running another tool."
- **Producer/auditor judging AC1** — "as the producer, I want the nightly
  report to carry the same figures the acceptance criteria are written
  against, so a claim in a work item can be checked against the report of the
  matching night."
- **Follow-on measurement items** — "as the agent implementing
  LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ, I want the nightly generator to emit these sections so
  the 24 h re-measurement is corroborated by the standard surface, not only by
  the standalone tool."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (stale rate section).** The nightly report renders a `slots_stale`
  section for its own window: status-poll count, polls with
  `slots_stale=true`, the rate, and the explicit outcome against a
  **configurable** stale-rate target (default < 5.0 % of polls). Polls
  without the `slots_stale` field (schema 1) are excluded from the
  denominator, never counted as fresh — the same derivation as
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`. The same figures are exposed as
  an additive `--json` key, and the section is omitted (no zero-fill) when the
  window has no status polls.
- **AC2 (capacity_hint distribution).** The nightly report renders the
  `capacity_hint` distribution — `idle` / `prefill_bound` / `saturated` counts
  **and shares** of status polls, including any unexpected token rather than
  dropping it — plus the `saturated`-without-live-work count (and its share of
  polls and of `saturated` polls), using the reference live-work derivation:
  `local_in_flight_requests > 0` for schema 3, with
  `local_active_query` / `active_query` as the schema-2 fallback. Exposed as
  an additive `--json` key.
- **AC3 (reproduction of the measured window).** Re-running the analyzer with
  `--start '2026-10-24 20:00:00' --end '2026-10-25 07:00:00'` reproduces the
  recorded figures in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/measurement.json`
  — 11,654 status polls; 9,278 stale (79.61 %); `idle` 4,577, `prefill_bound`
  6,024, `saturated` 1,053; 247 saturated-without-live-work — or every
  difference is explained in the work item (boundary semantics included; see
  Constraints). Verified as a test against the recorded artifact, not as a
  one-off manual run.
- **AC4 (tests).** New behaviour is covered by tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`: parser tests (synthetic
  `status_request` lines for schema 1/2/3, stale and fresh, with and without
  `local_in_flight_requests`) and rendering tests (section omitted on an empty
  window; counts, shares and target outcome asserted on a synthetic window;
  `--json` keys asserted). Tests pin the agreement with the reference
  derivation so the two surfaces cannot silently diverge. The full project
  test suite passes.
- **AC5 (documentation).** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and
  `REFERENCE.md` describe the new section and the additive `--json` keys, the
  target and how to override it, and the schema-2/3 live-work derivation —
  consistent with the `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` docstring it
  derives from.
- **AC6 (verification).** The nightly pipeline is run once over a closed
  window and the resulting `report.md` shows the new sections with figures that
  match the standalone tool for that window (recorded in the work item).

## Constraints

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` is **agent infrastructure**: editing it
  requires explicit operator authorisation for this work item — **granted**
  by the producer on 2026-10-29 (Appendix Q1). The authorisation covers an
  additive change to the report surface only; it is not a licence to
  restructure the skill.
- **Single implementation of the derivation.** Do not duplicate the reference
  tool's per-line field extraction, live-work derivation or stale-rate
  denominator: extract/reuse it so both surfaces agree by construction (AC3),
  with a test that fails if they diverge.
- **Window semantics must not drift.** The analyzer currently aggregates
  events with `window_start <= ts <= window_end` (closed interval), while the
  reference tool uses `[since, until)` (half-open). The status-poll
  aggregation must adopt the reference half-open semantics (or the difference
  must be explicitly reconciled) so AC3 can match exactly.
- **The nightly run stays unattended.** No new network call, LLM call or
  interactive prompt; a window with no status polls must render a clean
  report, not fail the cron run.
- **Additive surface only.** Existing report sections, CSV artifacts and
  `--json` keys keep their meaning; nothing already published is renamed or
  changed in place. CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (ship skill owns it).
- **Scope creep guard:** attribution of stale polls by cache source/latency
  band and abandonment-event attribution are *not* in scope here; if they are
  wanted nightly, file a follow-on item rather than widening this one.

## Existing state

- Reference tool: `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK,
  completed). Pure helpers to reuse: `is_status_poll()`,
  `_status_fields()` (`capacity_hint|slots_stale|slots_detail_stale|
  available_slots|local_active_query|active_query|local_in_flight_requests|
  status_schema_version|latency_ms`), `has_live_local_work()`,
  `_latency_band()`, and the `evaluate()` target checks
  (`--stale-rate-target`, default 0.05; violations target 0).
- Nightly analyzer parses `status_request` lines already
  (`log_parser.LogEvent(status_request)` with `capacity_hint`,
  `status_schema_version`, `available_slots`, `total_slots`,
  `prefill_eta_seconds`) and stores them as
  `AnalysisResult.status_request_events`, but it does **not** parse
  `slots_stale` / `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`,
  `local_active_query` / `active_query` or `latency_ms`, and nothing computes
  a stale rate or a violation count.
- `reporting.py::_append_contention_prediction_section()` already prints a
  **count-only** `capacity_hint` line ("Payload's own claim (`capacity_hint`
  over status polls) ...") inside M1, and `--json` carries
  `denial_attribution.capacity_hint` plus top-level `status_capacity_hint` —
  counts only, no shares, no violations, no stale rate.
- Recorded artifact for AC3 exists and is covered:
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/measurement.json`
  (`coverage.covered = true`, `window_end_gap_seconds = 2.0`) with the figures
  quoted in AC3; the tool re-verified them during the 2026-10-29 audit in ~9 s.
- The proxy emits the needed fields at schema 3
  (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, `status_extra`: `slots_stale`,
  `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`, `local_active_query`,
  `active_query`, `latency_ms`, `capacity_hint`, `status_schema_version`).
- Skill scripts are self-contained today (only their own directory on
  `sys.path`), but repo-level shared helpers are the established pattern
  (`scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`), and the skill's tests already load repo
  `scripts/` modules by file path with a documented `sys.path` dance
  (`tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py`). The 05:00 cron runs from the
  repo root, so a repo-level shared module is reachable.

## Desired change

1. One shared implementation of the status-poll derivations in
   `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`, imported by both
   `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` (natively, like
   `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`) and the nightly analyzer (through a small
   documented path-based shim), so the numbers agree by construction
   (placement decided: Appendix Q2).
2. A new nightly report section (`## Local capacity signals`, rendered after
   the contention-prediction section) with: poll count; stale count/rate and
   target outcome; the `capacity_hint` counts/shares; the
   saturated-without-live-work count and shares; and a one-line verdict that
   names each unmet target instead of burying it.
3. Additive `--json` keys (e.g. `capacity_signals.slots_stale`,
   `.capacity_hint`, `.saturated_without_live_work`, `.targets`) mirroring the
   section, so automation can read what the Markdown shows.
4. A configurable stale-rate target — a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on
   `analyze_proxy_usage.py` with the reference tool's 0.05 default (mechanism
   decided: Appendix Q3) — surfaced in the section and in `--json`.
5. Tests for parser + aggregation + rendering + JSON + agreement with the
   reference derivation, and a reproduction test for AC3's window.

Verification commands (copy-paste, run from the repo root):

```bash
# AC3 — the nightly analyzer over the recorded post-fix night window
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
    --start '2026-10-24 20:00:00' --end '2026-10-25 07:00:00' \
    --output-dir /tmp/capacity-signals-check

# the reference figures for that window (already recorded)
python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py \
    --since '2026-10-24 20:00' --until '2026-10-25 07:00' --window-closed \
    --label post-fix-night --json
```

## Plan (2026-10-30)

Decomposed into five children (all `stage=intake_complete`, ready for
`/skill:implement`), wired in dependency order:

| # | Child | Type | Priority | Depends on | Parent ACs delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | slots_stale rate published end-to-end in nightly report (**LP-0MVU8O4EL005IYP9**) | feature | high | — | AC1 (+ AC3/AC4 support) |
| 2 | capacity_hint distribution and saturated-without-live-work published in nightly report (**LP-0MVU8O9OC005YQU1**) | feature | high | 1 | AC2 (+ AC4 support) |
| 3 | Reproduce recorded 2026-10-24 post-fix night figures in the nightly analyzer (**LP-0MVU8OA1A002GTN0**) | task | medium | 1, 2 | AC3 |
| 4 | Document capacity-signal section, JSON keys and stale-rate target (**LP-0MVU8OF6K006ECQ9**) | docs | low | 1, 2 | AC5 |
| 5 | Verify nightly pipeline over a closed window against the standalone tool (**LP-0MVU8OFHH00987IW**) | task | medium | 1, 2 | AC6 |

Execution order: **1 → 2 → {3, 4, 5}**.

### Phasing decision (vertical slices)

Each implementation child is a **vertical slice through every layer** — shared
derivation (`scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`) → parser → aggregation → report
section → `--json` key → CLI flag → tests → doc rows — ending in a rendered
section, not a horizontal "parser only" or "aggregation only" step.

The item is Small effort, so it is delivered in two implementation slices rather
than a multi-phase programme: slice 1 cuts the tracer bullet with the
`slots_stale` rate (including the shared-module extraction and the
`--stale-rate-target` flag), slice 2 widens the same section to the
`capacity_hint` distribution and the saturated-without-live-work violations.
Children 3 and 5 are verification slices and child 4 is the consolidated docs
pass. Between slices the next child's description is reviewed and updated
before it is started.

### Test-first ordering (documented deviation)

The skill asks for test/verification children created before implementation
children. Every slice here is implemented **TDD within the slice** — failing
tests first, then the production change, then a single green commit — because
the repo gate forbids committing a red tree, so a standalone "tests only" child
could not land ahead of the code it exercises. The shared-derivation parity test
lives in slice 1 (which precedes everything else), and the verification children
(3, 5) are ordered as early as their dependencies allow.

### Duplicate check

`wl search "capacity_hint slots_stale nightly report"` (2026-10-30): no
completed item already publishes these figures nightly. LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK
(completed) is the standalone reference tool whose derivations this item reuses
— a semantic dependency, not a duplicate. No child was closed or rewritten for
overlap.

### Review stages applied

Six automated review stages plus the AC coverage review were run over this plan
(requirements/AC alignment, completeness incl. `**Key Files:**` validation,
sequencing and dependencies, scope sizing, acceptance/testability, polish). The
single gap found — the parent's scope-creep guard (no stale-poll attribution by
cache source/latency band) was not stated in any child — was closed by an
"Out of scope" section on child 1. AC coverage review: 100 % of parent ACs
covered by children.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 (session `herdr-1793320181-2789500-21575`): five children created
  in dependency order; AC1/AC2 slices ordered first, verification (AC3/AC6) and
  docs (AC5) after them; child 1 gained the scope-creep guard section. No change
  to the item's intent, ACs, constraints or decisions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parse
  `slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale`, `local_in_flight_requests`,
  `local_active_query` / `active_query`, `latency_ms` on `status_request`
  events (additive `LogEvent` fields, `None` on pre-change lines).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — status-poll
  aggregation (counts, half-open window filter, hint histogram, violations)
  feeding the new section/JSON.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — new
  `## Local capacity signals` section + additive JSON keys.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — stale-rate
  target option (if Q3 chooses a flag).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — new `test_capacity_signals.py`
  (parser/aggregation/render/JSON/agreement/reproduction).
- `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` — **new** home of the shared status-poll
  derivation (field extraction, live-work rule, stale denominator, hint
  histogram, target checks), imported by both surfaces (Q2).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — reference implementation; drops
  its private copies in favour of the shared module without changing its
  published figures.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md` — document the
  section, keys and target.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decided (Q1, 2026-10-29):** the operator authorises edits under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` for this item, restricted to the
  additive report surface described here.
- **Assumption:** the section belongs in the standard report rather than a new
  artifact, and is rendered after the contention-prediction section; both are
  additive and reversible, and no existing section parser keys off section
  order (checked: only `tests/test_contention_prediction.py` splits on its own
  heading).
- **Risk (window boundary):** an inclusive-end analyzer window would count
  polls the reference tool excludes, breaking exact AC3 reproduction. Mitigated
  by adopting half-open semantics for status polls and by a boundary test with
  a poll at exactly `end`.
- **Risk (divergent copies):** extracting the helpers can leave a stale copy
  in either surface. Mitigated by a test that asserts both surfaces produce
  identical figures on the same synthetic lines.
- **Risk (report noise):** a 24 h window makes the stale rate easy to
  misread as capacity truthfulness. The section text must repeat the reference
  tool's caveat: the stale rate is a *polling-path* signal and is only
  meaningful with the build it was measured on.
- **Risk (unexpected vocabulary):** a future `capacity_hint` token must appear
  as its own row rather than being dropped or silently bucketed.
- **Risk (cron breakage):** a log window with no status polls (or no logs) must
  render an empty/absent section, not raise — the nightly run is unattended.
- **Risk (silent truncation):** unlike the reference tool, the nightly analyzer
  has no coverage-gap verdict, so a window whose retained logs are incomplete
  would publish a plausible-but-partial rate. The AC3 comparison must record
  that the reference run reported `coverage.covered = true` for the window,
  and the section must state when the poll count is derived from logs that do
  not span the whole window (or the limitation must be documented).

## Related work

- **LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK** (completed) — the standalone verification tool whose
  derivations this item publishes.
- **LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0** (open, plan_complete) — parent measurement whose AC1
  (`slots_stale` < 5 %, `saturated` only with live work) needs a nightly
  counterpart.
- **LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23** (completed) — publishing work this item was
  discovered from; the hand cross-check gap.
- **LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV** (open, plan_complete) — post-fix night measurement
  supplying the AC3 reference artifact.
- **LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ**, **LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ** (open) — successor
  re-measurements that would otherwise each need another ad-hoc tool run;
  LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ records AC3 as "partial: attribution complete but not in
  the nightly generator", which this item addresses for the capacity figures.
- **LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB** (in-progress) — abandoned-dispatch/cooldown bug that
  can move the violation count; not a dependency, but it must be recorded when
  comparing night to night.
- Reference artifact:
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/` (`REPORT.md`,
  `measurement.json`, `measurement.txt`).

## Decisions (interview answers recorded in the Appendix)

- **D1 (Q1, answered 2026-10-29):** operator authorisation to edit
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` is **granted** for this item, limited to
  the additive report surface.
- **D2 (Q2):** the shared derivation lives in
  `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`; the standalone tool imports it natively,
  the skill loads it through a documented path-based shim.
- **D3 (Q3):** the stale-rate target is a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py`, default 0.05.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Is operator authorisation granted to edit
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` for this work item?**
  Options: (a) authorised for this item; (b) not authorised — keep the change
  outside the skill; (c) authorised, but the change must be reviewed by the
  producer before it is pushed to `dev`.
  **Recommended:** (a) authorised for this item — the constraint exists to
  protect agent infrastructure, and the change is additive to the report
  only; (c) is the fallback if the operator wants a review gate.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29, interactive reply): "1. a" — authorised
  for this item.** Source: producer reply in the intake session. Scope read:
  the authorisation covers the additive report change described here (parser
  fields, aggregation, new section and JSON keys, tests, docs), not a
  restructure of the skill.

- **Q2: Where should the single shared derivation live so both surfaces agree
  by construction?**
  Options: (a) extract pure helpers into `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`;
  the standalone tool imports it natively, the skill loads it through a small
  documented path-based shim (precedent:
  `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py`); (b) the analyzer shells out to
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py --json`; (c) implement inside the
  skill and have the standalone tool import the skill module; (d) two
  implementations plus a cross-check test.
  **Recommended:** (a) — one implementation, repo convention for shared
  helpers (`scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`), no subprocess or coverage-model
  coupling, and the cron already runs from the repo root.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29, interactive reply): "2. a" — extract the
  pure helpers into `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`.** The skill reaches it
  through the documented path shim already used by
  `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py`.

- **Q3: How should the stale-rate target be configured?**
  Options: (a) a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on `analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  default 0.05, mirroring the reference tool; (b) a key in
  `proxy/config.yaml` read through `config_loader`; (c) both (flag overrides
  config).
  **Recommended:** (a) — matches the reference tool's surface, needs no
  config-schema change, and the cron line can carry an override if the target
  ever moves.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29, interactive reply): "3. a" — a new
  `--stale-rate-target` flag, default 0.05.**

## Headline

The 05:00 nightly report gains a `slots_stale` rate (against a configurable
< 5 % target) and a full `capacity_hint` distribution including
`saturated`-without-live-work, derived from one shared implementation with
`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` and verified by reproducing the
recorded 2026-10-24 post-fix night figures (11,654 polls / 79.61 % / 247
violations).

## Problem statement

The free-slot (direct-dispatch) admission guard in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` already records the governing decision reason verbatim for the deadline, deadline-relative safety-budget and flat cold-prefill-budget refusals (shipped with LP-0MVQ23API001UOET, commit `0466f5db`), but **no test pins that behaviour on the direct path**: the reason-contract tables drive only `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` through the free-slot route, so a regression could silently restore the 2026-10-25 retry-storm shape — a `Retry-After` advertised for a prompt that waiting cannot heal — whenever a local slot happens to be free.

## Users

- **Proxy operators / on-call engineers.** Story: *As an on-call engineer reading `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` and a client `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, I want the token to name the bound that actually refused local, so I can tell a temporal refusal (wait) from a permanent one (compact) without cross-referencing the guard's internal logic.*
- **Local-preferred clients (agents).** Story: *As an agent that is pinned local, I want a `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusal to say `retryable: false` and never hand me a `Retry-After`, so I compact my prompt instead of re-driving the same over-budget request in a retry loop.*
- **Proxy maintainers.** Story: *As a maintainer, I want both dispatch paths (queue and free-slot) covered by one table-driven contract, so adding a refusal reason cannot land with retry semantics on one path only.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Direct-path reason pass-through is table-driven and complete.** `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` drives every admission-guard reason through the **free-slot** (direct) path end-to-end via `proxy_with_fallback` — `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, and the ETA/budget case — asserting both `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` and body `reason` equal the governing decision reason, with `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` used only where the free-slot ETA/budget bound itself is the cause.
2. **A free-slot over-budget request refuses without a timer.** With a free local slot and a prompt above `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, the end-to-end refusal through `proxy_with_fallback` carries `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`, no `Retry-After` header, `retryable: false`, `suggested_action` naming compaction, and the token evidence (`new_tokens` / `budget_tokens`) on both headers and body.
3. **The governing reason reaches the recorded attempt and the dispatch log.** The `local_admission_reject` attempt diagnostics and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback ... reason=<token>` log line name the governing reason (not `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) for the deadline, safety-budget and cold-budget refusals; the line still carries `free_slot=true`.

data.description:
## Problem statement

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout to the commit it is
about to push (main checkout dirty from concurrent work), it logs a warning and pushes
anyway from that stale checkout. The `dev`/`main` push then runs `.githooks/pre-push`
with `--project-root <main checkout>` — so the full suite is measured against the *old*
working tree, and the result is cached under the *old* git-state fingerprint
(`HEAD` + dirty content). The push returns green in seconds without the pushed commit
ever being verified: a silent fail-open in the only full-suite enforcement point for
`dev`.

## Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main
  checkout: they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused, never
  a green gate that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without
  re-running the suite manually.*

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — fail closed on a stale checkout.** For a push targeting `refs/heads/dev` or `refs/heads/main`, the hook compares the gated `local_sha` (already on stdin) with the `HEAD` of the tree it is about to measure; on mismatch it **refuses the push before the suite runs**, and the message names the pushed commit, the checked-out `HEAD`, the tree path and the recovery steps. It never reports green using evidence from a different tree.
- **AC2 — fail closed on a dirty tree.** When `HEAD` matches the pushed commit but the tree has uncommitted/untracked changes, the gate also refuses (project-declared expected-dirty paths, if any, are excluded) — a dirty fingerprint can never equal the pushed commit's clean fingerprint, so a green run there is not evidence about the pushed commit.
- **AC3 — evidence at the pushed commit.** A green `dev` push from a clean checkout at the pushed commit still leaves a full-suite cache entry keyed to that commit (`run_tests.py --summary` reports it), i.e. the guard adds a precondition, not a different cache key.
- **AC4 — regression test.** `tests/test_git_hooks.py` reproduces "dirty main checkout / skipped fast-forward" (pushed `local_sha` ≠ checkout `HEAD`, and separately a dirty tree at the matching `local_sha`) in the existing hermetic sandbox, asserting the push is refused, both SHAs appear in the message, and the runner is **never invoked**; the existing green `dev`-push and feature-branch-skip tests still pass.
- **AC5 — documentation.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents the pushed-commit contract, the refusal conditions and messages, the recovery path, a copy-pasteable reproduction (mismatched-sha simulation), and that `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` / `--no-verify` remain the explicit escape hatches.
- At least one test/validation criterion is covered by the repo suite; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope decided (Q1 = A): repo-local only.** The change lands in this repository —
  `.githooks/pre-push`, `tests/test_git_hooks.py`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`. No
  agent-infrastructure file is edited: `implement.py` (Step 5/6), `test_cache.py` and the
  canonical hook copies in `projects/SorraAgents` are **out of scope** and are recorded as
  a framework follow-up (see *Related work*). Because the hook runs for every `dev` push,
  the fail-closed guard fixes the observable defect for this repo without touching the
  framework.
- `.githooks/pre-push` must stay POSIX `sh` with no new runtime dependencies.
- **Q3 = B (strict):** both a `HEAD` ≠ `local_sha` mismatch and a dirty tree at the
  matching commit refuse the push; the escape hatches (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`,
  `--no-verify`) keep working unchanged.
- Feature-branch pushes must keep skipping the suite (fast loop unchanged) — the guard
  applies only to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` targets.
- Cache plumbing stays fail-soft: mirroring must never decide a push's outcome.
- **Q2 = B (keep both items, one implementation):** this item and
  LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 (non-fast-forward retry path) share the *same* hook guard.
  Whichever is scheduled first implements the guard; the other becomes verification of
  its own trigger scenario only. No second copy of the guard.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` already reads all four stdin fields per pushed ref
  (`local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha`
  is discarded, so the gate cannot tell which commit it is supposed to verify.
- The gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  with `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — i.e. the checkout `git push`
  runs in, which `implement.py finish` makes the **main checkout**.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` fingerprints `HEAD` + the content of every dirty path,
  so a stale-but-dirty main checkout produces a *valid, different* fingerprint; a
  previous green run for that same stale+dirty state is a legitimate cache hit → the gate
  returns green in seconds.
- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit
  precisely so the hook sees the new files; on failure it only logs
  `"Fast-forward dev failed (%s); push will proceed from the stale checkout — the
  context-budget gate may reject the push."` and continues to Step 6
  (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`).
- The push path can also retry after a non-fast-forward rebase
  (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`), which pushes the rebased commit from the main
  checkout — the guarded condition is identical, which is why LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and
  this item share one implementation.
- Observed 2026-10-28 (LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND): main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths),
  fast-forward skipped, main `dev` stayed at `7393ef14`, push landed `11870e99`; gate
  green in seconds; `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit;
  a throwaway worktree at the pushed commit gave 6136 passed / 0 failed.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (13 hermetic sandbox tests, fake runner,
  behavioural assertions) — its `_hook()` helper always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so
  no test can express "pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree"; `--strict-git-env` runs are
  driven through the fake runner, so the new tests need no real suite.

## Desired change

Add a **fail-closed pushed-commit guard** to the `dev`/`main` gate in
`.githooks/pre-push`:

1. While reading stdin, capture the `local_sha` of every gated ref
   (`refs/heads/dev|main`), ignoring deletion pushes (all-zero sha).
2. Before running the suite, resolve the gate tree (`repo_root`) and compare its
   `git rev-parse HEAD` with the captured `local_sha`. On mismatch → refuse with an
   actionable message (pushed sha, checkout `HEAD`, tree path, "re-run
   `implement.py finish` from a clean main checkout, or verify the commit in a worktree
   and re-push").
3. Refuse when the tree is dirty (excluding declared expected-dirty paths) even if the
   `HEAD` matches, because no green run there is evidence about the pushed commit.
4. Keep the existing behaviour otherwise: the suite still runs with
   `--scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`, cache mirroring intact,
   feature-branch pushes untouched, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` still bypassing the gate (and the
   guard) explicitly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — capture the gated `local_sha` in the stdin loop (currently
  discarded, `while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`); add the
  mismatch + dirty checks and their refusal messages inside the
  `need_full_suite = 1` gate block; leave `mirror_suite_cache` and the worklog-sync tail
  alone.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — extend `_hook()` with a `local_sha` override (default
  `HEAD`) and a dirty-tree setup; new tests for (a) `local_sha` ≠ `HEAD` refused with
  both SHAs named and `_marker()` empty, (b) dirty tree at matching `local_sha` refused,
  (c) clean matching tree still runs the full suite (existing coverage keeps passing),
  (d) feature-branch push with a mismatched sha still skips the suite.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — new subsection "The gate verifies the pushed commit" with the
  refusal conditions, messages, recovery, and the reproduction recipe (`printf
  '<local-ref> <local-sha> <remote-ref> <zero-sha>
' | sh .githooks/pre-push …` with a
  sha that is not `HEAD`); keep the existing simulate-a-push recipe consistent.
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — no logic change expected (it only sets
  `core.hooksPath` and repairs the exec bit); confirm it stays a no-op for this change.
- Framework follow-up (out of scope, not edited here):
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (Step 5 ~5141–5216, Step 6 push
  ~5235, finish report) and `~/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 — "dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the
  non-fast-forward retry path" (open, bug).** Shares the identical invariant and the
  same hook guard (its AC1: "a mismatch between the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed
  `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree: gate it correctly or refuse with
  an actionable message"). Per Q2 = B the guard is implemented **once** under whichever
  item is scheduled first; the other becomes verification of its own trigger scenario.
- LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND — discovering item (post-push verification of its dev push
  surfaced the gap).
- LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ — "Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout
  (`core.hooksPath` unset)" — the gate's activation history and the same
  `run_tests.py --summary` = `missing` signal.
- LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK — activated `core.hooksPath` and pinned the context-budget
  thresholds (the gate family this item hardens).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the gate's contract, escape hatches and the
  "simulate a `dev` push" recipe.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the
  main checkout by design; the reason the framework alternative (Q1 option C) was not
  taken.

## Risks & assumptions

- *Risk: fail-closed blocks a finish whenever the main checkout is dirty or stale.* That
  is the intended release-gate behaviour; the refusal message names the one-step recovery
  (clean the main checkout and re-run `implement.py finish`), and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` /
  `--no-verify` remain explicit escapes. The main checkout of this repo is clean at
  intake time, so routine finishes are unaffected.
- *Risk: false refusal on legitimate multi-ref pushes.* Mitigation: the guard evaluates
  only `refs/heads/dev|main` targets and ignores deletion (all-zero) shas; tests cover a
  feature-branch ref sharing the same push.
- *Risk: the guard is bypassed by a push that never runs the hook* (`--no-verify`).
  Out of scope — documented escape hatch, not silently allowed.
- *Risk: scope creep into the framework.* The framework half (finish report naming the
  verified tree, pushing from the worktree, propagating the guard to every consumer
  repo's hook copy) stays a linked follow-up, not part of this item.
- *Assumption: the cache fingerprint semantics stay as-is* (`HEAD` + dirty content); the
  guard makes the precondition match the fingerprint rather than redefining the key.
- *Assumption: `implement.py` keeps pushing from the main checkout*, so a skipped
  fast-forward now surfaces as a refused push with an actionable message instead of a
  silent green gate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Evidence gathered before asking (so the questions were not repo-search answerable):
`.githooks/pre-push` discards `local_sha`; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on
`HEAD` + dirty content; `implement.py` Step 5 only *warns* when the fast-forward is
skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always
sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`; the main checkout of this repo is clean.

- **Q1 (shape + scope).** Which fix shape, in which repository?
  - A: repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` + regression test; framework
    improvement as a linked follow-up.
  - B: repo-local "gate the pushed commit" via a throwaway detached worktree at
    `local_sha`.
  - C: framework-only change (`implement.py`), requiring agent-infrastructure
    authorisation.
  - **Recommended:** A.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): A** — repo-local fail-closed
    guard in `.githooks/pre-push`, with the framework follow-up kept out of scope.
- **Q2 (overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3).**
  - A: transfer this item's distinct ACs onto that item and close this as duplicate.
  - B: keep both; implement the shared guard once under whichever is scheduled first and
    link the other as verification-only.
  - **Recommended:** B.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): B** — both items stay; one
    implementation of the guard, the other item verifies its own trigger.
- **Q3 (strictness when `HEAD` == `local_sha` but the tree is dirty).**
  - A: run the gate anyway with a warning.
  - B: refuse — a dirty fingerprint can never match the pushed commit's clean
    fingerprint, so `run_tests.py --summary` at the pushed commit stays `missing`.
  - **Recommended:** B (excluding project-declared expected-dirty paths; none declared
    here).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): B** — refuse on a dirty tree as
    well as on a HEAD mismatch.

## Goal

The direct free-slot local-only refusal is produced by _build_local_admission_reject_response (via _build_exhausted_response) rather than the pin-local refusal builder, and the wiring slice LP-0MVSMINPR006SWT6 deliberately left that payload unchanged (boundary). Consequently that 429 body carries no verdict key, and the matrix row admission_guard_free_slot is scoped out of the verdict assertion in test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py (skip, documented at _VERDICT_NOT_APPLICABLE).

## Deliverable (proposal)

Decide the singular implementation for the admission-reject payload, then wire admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict into it (one call, sharing the single-implementation contract) or route the free-slot branch through _build_local_only_refusal_response; add verdict to that 429 body, promote the matrix row by deleting _VERDICT_NOT_APPLICABLE, and cover the log/body assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria (proposed)

- AC1 The admission-reject 429 body carries verdict=deferrable|too_large consistent with the shared helper, with no existing field or header changed.
- AC2 provider.py still holds exactly one verdict computation (no second table/estimator).
- AC3 The matrix row admission_guard_free_slot asserts body[verdict] == 'deferrable' (no skip); changed-scope gate green.

## Constraints

- Retry timing unchanged; no promotion to remote; follow the wiring slice's D1-D8 reasoning where applicable.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator evaluating the 60 s → 30 s contention-queue sweep
(LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R), I want a windowed report that separates ticket-backed
dispatches, residual queue wins and residual queue losses (with a lease-active
`reason` split), so the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline and the post-flip verdict are
measured with one definition.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC3 (residual-queue telemetry) and
the AC1 trigger precondition (a ≥24 h baseline at 60 s / depth 8 must exist
before the sweep is applied).

## Scope

- New `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py`: CLI with `--log-dir`, a
  stated window (`--since`/`--until` or `--hours`), `--sweep-budget-seconds`
  (default 30), `--json` and a human/markdown render; modelled on
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`.
- Reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (`discover_proxy_log_files`,
  `parse_line_timestamp`, `iter_proxy_log_lines`) and import
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a **read-only**
  library where practical (never edit that skill's files).
- Report sections for the window:
  (a) ticket-backed dispatches — `local_admission_reserve_claimed` count
      (reported, **not** a flip gate);
  (b) residual queue wins — `contention_queue_dispatch ... queued_duration=`,
      count, share at or below the sweep budget, and a wait distribution
      (p50/p75/p90/max);
  (c) residual queue losses — `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue ...
      queued_duration=`, count, aggregate wait, wait-per-hour, and a split by
      `reason` (`local_lease_active` vs `none`/other).
- Only the two lease-retention emit sites carry `reason=local_lease_active`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~12312 and ~12358); a missing `reason=` is
  counted as `none`, never dropped.
- Exit codes mirror `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`: 0 = measurement complete,
  2 = incomplete (no logs / thin window / coverage gap; never silently pass),
  1 = invalid input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC3 — residual-queue telemetry.** A windowed report (script + test) emits
   ticket-backed dispatches, residual wins and residual losses split by reason.
2. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py --log-dir <dir> --hours 24`
   prints a report containing all three sections (ticket-backed count, win
   count/share/distribution, loss count/aggregate wait/reason split) for the
   stated window; `--json` emits the same numbers machine-readably.
3. Unit tests in `tests/test_contention_queue_sweep_report.py` drive the CLI
   against synthetic proxy-log fixtures (mixed wins/losses, lease-active and
   reason-less losses, empty window, window filtering) and assert every
   section, the reason split, the at-or-below-budget share, and the 0/2/1 exit
   codes — no live logs required.
4. The report is run against the available ≥24 h pre-flip window at 60 s /
   depth 8 and its numbers (queue events/h, wins, losses, aggregate dead wait,
   lease-active vs none split, ticket count) are recorded as a comment on this
   item and summarised on LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R.
5. A short runbook `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep.md` documents the
   invocation, the three sections, the exit codes and the baseline numbers.
6. Changed-scope tests for the new script and its log parsing pass.

## Constraints

- Log events are the telemetry contract: **no new status counters**
  (`LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` removed the cumulative ones on purpose).
- Read-only use of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`; that skill is not edited.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new)
- `tests/test_contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new)
- `docs/dev/contention-queue-sweep.md` (new)
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (reuse: discovery + timestamps)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (read-only import)

## Dependencies

- None upstream.
- Its baseline must be recorded before the sweep child is applied (parent AC1
  trigger: ≥24 h 60 s / depth 8 baseline).

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the contention queue to be a bounded straggler net
(30 s, depth 2) instead of a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops
competing with real local work, while a slot that frees within seconds is
still usable.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC2 (single-source budget) and
AC4 (tests/validation).

## Change

```yaml
contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
```

Evidence (proxy.log*, 2026-10-22 19:00→22:18, 3.3 h at 60 s / depth 8): 180
queue events — 38 wins (21 %) / 142 losses (79 %), every loss at the full
60 s, 8 705 s aggregate dead wait; wins retained by budget: 20 s → 24 %,
30 s → 34 %, 45 s → 60 %. Trigger, flip criteria and the two-line rollback
live on the parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, flip criteria and rollback.
2. `proxy/config.yaml` ships 30 s / depth 2 and the surrounding comment block
   (~lines 1740-1800) records the new evidence, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline
   requirement, the 7-day observation window, the three flip criteria and the
   two-line rollback (revert to 60 / 8, restart the proxy).
3. **AC2 — single-source budget.** The shortened budget reaches the admission
   guard and the reservation endpoint through one resolver
   (`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds`); no second constant, no per-call
   default. Tests assert `wait_budget_seconds(merged config, "medium") ==
   30.0`, the guard's refusal payload and `X-Local-Admission-Budget` header
   report 30 s, `POST /llama/local/reserve` prices against the same 30 s, and
   `high` priority still resolves to 0 s — all through
   `_get_contention_queue_config`.
4. depth 2 is accepted unchanged; clamping happens only outside [1, 16]
   (values 1 and 16 pass through unchanged).
5. **AC4 — tests / validation.** Unit tests cover the swept values end to end:
   resolver 30 s, depth 2, 30 s timeout. A third waiter with 2 parked falls
   back immediately without enqueueing, and a parked waiter that is not
   served falls back at 30 s (tiny/mocked caps — never a real 30 s sleep).
6. Stale fixtures/tests that assert the shipped 60 s / 8 defaults are updated
   (`proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py::test_{cheap,fast}_config_declares_queue_policy`
   and any other shipped-config assertions), not left stale. The code-level
   defaults for a missing key stay as the inert no-config fallback and are
   documented as such (absent queue key ⇒ policy `fallback` ⇒ nothing queues).
7. Code comments in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (module docstring still says
   60 s), `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` and `proxy/proxy/router.py`
   state the single-budget contract; no behavioural change beyond the two
   config values.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated ⇒
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget.
- Out of scope: queue removal, slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model,
  client reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- The config change requires a proxy restart; deployment happens in the
  observation child after a quiet-window restart, not in this item's session.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the report/baseline child: the ≥24 h 60 s / depth 8 baseline must
  be recorded before this sweep is applied.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the queue documented as a bounded straggler safety net
for non-cooperating clients, with reservations as the primary cooperative
path, so the 30 s / depth 2 values and the 60 → 30 / 8 → 2 change are
explained and cannot drift from the shipped config.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers parent AC5 (docs) and the documentation
half of AC6.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC5 — docs.** `proxy/config.yaml` comments and `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   describe the queue as a straggler net; 30 s / depth 2 recorded.
2. **AC6 — documentation & suite.** All related documentation is updated to
   the new values and the full suite passes.
3. `proxy/docs/routing.md` describes reservations (`POST /llama/local/reserve`,
   `X-Local-Reservation` / `X-Local-Preference`) as the primary cooperative
   path; every queue table/value in the file (currently 60 s / depth 8 at
   ~674, ~731, ~897-899) states 30 s / depth 2.
4. The change is recorded with its measurement dates (2026-10-22 3.3 h intake
   window; ≥24 h pre-flip baseline), the three flip criteria, and the
   two-line rollback (revert to 60 / 8 + proxy restart), citing
   LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R.
5. `README.md`'s per-priority contention-queue section (~lines 230-267, today
   stale at depth 8 / wait 120 s) shows the shipped 30 s / depth 2 and the
   straggler-net framing, pointing at `proxy/docs/routing.md`.
6. A drift test (`proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_docs.py`, pattern:
   `proxy/tests/test_idle_admit_config_docs.py`) asserts the shipped config
   values and the key phrases appear in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and
   `README.md`, so a future value change cannot leave the docs stale.
7. No contradictory queue numbers remain in the touched files (`grep` for
   `120s`, `depth 8` and `60 s` queue references is clean).

## Key Files

- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `README.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_docs.py` (new drift test)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (comment cross-reference only)

  recorded change).

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

## Goal

As an implementer of the GPU telemetry slices (parent LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W) I need
shared, deterministic verification assets — `/slots` payload fixtures, recorded
Prometheus HTTP API payloads, and a `gpu_busy_percent` guard that also covers the
new CLI — so every later child starts from a failing test instead of from code.

## Context

This is the **test-first slice** of the parent plan. It changes no production
behaviour: it delivers the verification harness that the sampler (sibling
"Publish slot occupancy metrics from the proxy"), the recording rule (sibling
"Combined computing-workload recording rule") and the CLI (sibling
"`gpu_utilisation` CLI with honest unknown share") consume.

Live evidence gathered while planning (2026-10-29, this host): the deployed
llama.cpp build answers `GET :8080/slots?model=mxbai-embed` with
`[{"id":0,"n_ctx":256,"speculative":false,"is_processing":false}, ...]` — no
`id_task` and no `next_token` while idle. Fixtures must therefore cover both this
build's shape and the older/richer shape that carries `id_task`/`next_token`.
`curl localhost:8000/slots` returns 404 (the proxy does not expose `/slots`), as
the parent brief states.

## Minimal implementation

- Add fixtures next to the tests that use them (`proxy/tests/`, pytest `conftest.py`
  or a small `gpu_fixtures.py` helper) — payload builders, not golden blobs, so a
  case is one keyword argument away.
- Record Prometheus API payloads as JSON under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` with a
  small README line saying how each was captured (endpoint + query + window).
- Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` scanning in
  `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` to include `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reusable fixtures exist for a healthy `/slots` payload (mixed `is_processing`), an empty payload, a richer payload carrying `id_task`/`next_token`, and failed fetches (HTTP 500, timeout, connection error) — each fixture is asserted to have the shape its consumer expects.
- [ ] Recorded `query_range` payloads exist under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` for `gpu:computing:bool`, `gpu:computing_workload:bool`, `gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and `up{job="llama-proxy"|"node-exporter"}`, including one stream with a deliberate gap of missing samples; each file documents the endpoint, query and window it was captured from.
- [ ] The `gpu_busy_percent` guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` also scans `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` and fails if the series appears in any query expression, while still allowing documentation/comment mentions.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that the guard fails on a synthetic expression containing `gpu_busy_percent` and passes on the real files (the guard must not be vacuously green).
- [ ] Every test asserts observable behaviour (fixture shape, guard outcome, exact split), not merely that a value is non-`None`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/conftest.py` / `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` (new or extended)
- `monitoring/tests/fixtures/slots_api_responses.json` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_telemetry_sampler.py` (fixture consumers land here later)

## Notes

Keep this slice small: only fixtures and guards that at least one sibling child
actually consumes. If a sibling ends up needing a different shape, extend the
fixture in that child rather than pre-building speculative variants.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need the proxy to publish **slot occupancy** (total slots, busy
slots, per-slot 0/1 state, in-flight tasks and the age of the last successful
sample) on its existing `/metrics` endpoint, so that "GPU power was high" can be
attributed to llama-server work and gaps in the sample stream stay visible.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W. This child is the **workload half** of the parent:
Power/VRAM/GTT already arrive via node_exporter (`gpu-metrics.service` +
`gpu_compute_rules.yaml`), but nothing publishes slot state — verified
2026-10-29: `curl localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_slots_` returns only the
existing `llama_slots_query_failures_total` / `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total`
counters, and `curl localhost:8000/slots` is 404.

Reuse, do not rebuild:

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py::_fetch_slots_payload` — TTL caching (1 s),
  single-flight coalescing, bounded follower wait, failure backoff (5 s).
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py::_query_slots_detail` — per-slot
  `slot_id` / `is_processing` extraction (returns `[]` on failure, so the
  sampler must not treat that as "zero slots").
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_resolve_local_slots_target` — child-port
  discovery plus the throttled fallback counter, so the sampler does not traverse
  the router and re-introduce the cancel-500 behaviour (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — the existing optional-`prometheus_client` pattern
  (module-level `None` gauges, guarded registration, no-op when the library is
  absent).

Known trap: a failed query must produce **no gauge write at all** (absent/stale),
never `llama_slots_busy 0`. The heartbeat
`llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` is what makes staleness queryable.

## Minimal implementation

- New gauges in `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`: `llama_slots_total`,
  `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slot_busy{slot="<id>"}`, `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks`,
  `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds`; register under the same `if _enabled:` guard.
- New `record_slot_occupancy(snapshot | None)` helper plus a
  `_slot_metrics_loop()` task in `observability.py` (or `backends/llama.py`),
  started from the proxy lifespan only when metrics are enabled; interval from
  `server.llama_slot_metrics_interval_seconds` (default 10 s, documented in
  `proxy/config.yaml` next to the wedge-detector keys).
- Remove per-slot labels for slots no longer present in the payload, so a
  restarted llama-server does not leave ghost `slot=` series.
- `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks` = slots that report an assigned task: count
  `id_task >= 0` when the build publishes it, else count `is_processing: true`
  (this build publishes no `id_task` — verify live and document the fallback in
  the metric docstring).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC1 (restated in full):** The proxy publishes slot occupancy series on `/metrics` — total slots, busy-slot count, per-slot 0/1 busy state, in-flight task count and a last-successful-sample timestamp — refreshed by a sampler loop with a configurable interval (default 10 s); a failed `/slots` query leaves the metrics absent/stale rather than reporting zero busy slots, and the failure remains visible through the existing failure counter.
- [ ] The proxy publishes slot occupancy series on `/metrics` — total slots, busy-slot count, per-slot 0/1 busy state, in-flight task count and a last-successful-sample timestamp — refreshed by a sampler loop with a configurable interval (default 10 s); a failed `/slots` query leaves the metrics absent/stale rather than reporting zero busy slots, and the failure remains visible through the existing failure counter.
- [ ] The series are registered only when `prometheus_client` is importable, and a test proves the proxy still serves `/metrics` (and the sampler does not raise) when the library is absent.
- [ ] The sampler loop reuses the coalesced `/slots` path and child-port discovery (`_fetch_slots_payload` + `_resolve_local_slots_target`); no second HTTP client and no new listening port are introduced, and the /slots timeout budget stays ≤ the existing 2 s default.
- [ ] `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` advances only on a successful sample, so the age of the last successful slot sample is queryable and a stalled sampler is distinguishable from idle slots.
- [ ] Per-slot `slot=` labels are cleaned up when a slot disappears from the payload (asserted by a test that shrinks the slot count).
- [ ] Unit tests cover sampler interval configurability (config default and override), healthy publication of every gauge, failure → no write plus incremented `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason=...}`, heartbeat non-advance on failure, and the optional-client no-op path; each asserts observable values.
- [ ] On a live host `curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep '^llama_slots'` shows the new series with plausible values (recorded in the completion comment).
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (coalesced `/slots` path; loop lives here or in `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py`)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (see `_resolve_local_slots_target`, no change expected)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (`server.llama_slot_metrics_interval_seconds`)
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_telemetry_sampler.py` (new)
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` (must stay accurate — expected to need no change)

## Notes

Risk carried from the parent brief: a 10 s sampler adds load to an endpoint that
has produced 1 392 timeout failures on this host. Mitigation is reuse of the
coalesced path, the short timeout, and the configurable interval — do not add a
dedicated poller that bypasses coalescing.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator (or an agent writing PromQL) I need **one shared definition** of
"the GPU is doing our local model's work" — power at compute level *and* at least
one llama-server slot busy — expressed as a Prometheus recording rule, so the new
CLI, alerts and ad-hoc queries cannot drift into three different definitions.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC3). `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` already
records the power-only `gpu:computing:bool` (`gpu:power_watts:amdgpu >= bool 90`)
with `promtool` behavioural tests in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`. That
series is kept unchanged for comparison; this child adds the combined rule on top
of it and on `llama_slots_busy` published by the sibling sampler child.

**Label-matching trap (found while planning):** the two inputs come from
*different scrape jobs* — the power series carries `instance="localhost:9100"`
(node_exporter) and `llama_slots_busy` carries `instance="localhost:8000"`
(llama-proxy). A naive `and` / `on(instance)` join matches nothing and the rule
silently yields **no series at all** (which would look like "unknown" forever, or
in a dashboard like "never computing"). Use label-agnostic vector matching —
e.g. `gpu:computing:bool * on() group_left() (llama_slots_busy >= bool 1)`, or an
equivalent form — and prove it with a `promtool test rules` case whose input
series carry those distinct `instance` labels.

Keep the missing-data semantics: when `llama_slots_busy` is absent (sampler down,
proxy down) the rule must produce **no series**, not `0`. Absence is `unknown`,
and 0 is "idle" — conflating them is exactly what the parent forbids.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `gpu:computing_workload:bool` to `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` plus a
  header paragraph on the join semantics and the gap behaviour.
- Extend `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` with the cases below.
- No change to `monitoring/prometheus.yml` is expected (the rule file is already
  loaded); confirm with `promtool check config`.
- Do **not** add `gpu_busy_percent` anywhere (guard already enforces this).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC3 (restated in full):** Computing time is defined as `power >= 90 W AND at least one slot busy`, expressed once as a Prometheus recording rule that the CLI, alerts and ad-hoc PromQL all share (asserted by a `promtool test rules` case in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`); the output also shows the power-only fraction so the two definitions can be compared, and `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation (a regression test asserts no rule file or CLI expression uses it as a utilisation input).
- [ ] Computing time is defined as `power >= 90 W AND at least one slot busy`, expressed once as a Prometheus recording rule (`gpu:computing_workload:bool`) that the CLI, alerts and ad-hoc PromQL all share, with the existing power-only `gpu:computing:bool` preserved unchanged for comparison.
- [ ] A `promtool test rules` case in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` asserts the recording rule's 0/1 values, including a case whose input series carry the two different `instance` labels (`localhost:9100` power, `localhost:8000` slots) so a label-matching regression fails the test.
- [ ] Rule cases cover: power ≥ 90 W with 1+ busy slots → 1; power ≥ 90 W with 0 busy slots → 0; power < 90 W with busy slots → 0; power exactly at 90 W → 1 (boundary); missing `llama_slots_busy` → the recorded series is absent (not 0); missing power → absent.
- [ ] `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation: the rule file contains no reference to it, and the existing `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` regression test in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` still passes.
- [ ] `promtool check rules monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` and `promtool test rules monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` pass, and the rule-file header documents why absence must stay absent (no series rather than 0).

- `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`

## Goal

As an operator I can run one command — `python3 scripts/gpu_utilisation.py
--window 2h` — and read `computing 32.4% / idle 61.1% / unknown 6.5%, mean 61 W,
max 118 W, peak 3 busy slots`, with `--json` giving an agent the same numbers,
so "how busy was the GPU between 17:00 and 19:00?" is a direct measurement that
does not depend on `proxy.log`.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, and the output half of AC3).
The store is the deployed Prometheus (`127.0.0.1:9090`, 90 d retention, 15 s
scrape). A very similar (smaller) reader already exists at
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` — reuse its *approach*
(urllib + `/api/v1/query_range`, best-effort JSON, dataclass result) but do not
import from `.pi/` (agent infrastructure, out of bounds); put the code in
`scripts/` and keep the new module self-contained.

**The honesty requirement is the hard part.** `avg_over_time` renormalises over
present samples only, so a 2 h window where the sampler was down for 30 min
reports a *higher* computing fraction than reality and cannot distinguish "idle"
from "nobody was looking". Compute coverage explicitly and report the remainder
as `unknown`:

- expected samples = window length ÷ step (the step actually queried, reported in
  the output next to the 15 s scrape floor);
- present samples = union of the sentinels that prove the pipeline was alive at
  that instant: `up{job="llama-proxy"}`, `up{job="node-exporter"}` and the
  `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` heartbeat (a sample counts as *observed*
  only when it is fresh within one scrape interval of the evaluation instant);
- `computing` = observed samples where `gpu:computing_workload:bool == 1`;
  `idle` = observed samples where it is `0`; `unknown` = expected − observed.
  The three shares must sum to 100 % by construction (assert it).

Guard: `gpu_busy_percent` must never appear in any expression (the sibling
test-first child adds the guard that scans this file).

## Minimal implementation

- `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`: `argparse` (`--since`, `--until`, `--window`,
  `--step`, `--prometheus-url`, `--json`), window/step resolution, one place
  holding the query expressions (`QUERIES` dict), arithmetic, human + JSON output.
- Reuse the recorded payloads from `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` in tests rather
  than hitting a live Prometheus; inject the HTTP getter so tests need no network.
- Report both definitions: `computing_pct` (workload rule) and
  `power_only_computing_pct` (`gpu:computing:bool`), plus `peak_busy_slots`
  (`max_over_time(llama_slots_busy[window])`) and `mean`/`max` power.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC2 (restated in full):** `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` reports, for an arbitrary window (`--since/--until` or `--window`, `--step`), the computing-time percentage, idle percentage, unknown percentage, mean and max power in watts, and peak concurrent busy slots; `--json` emits the same figures machine-readably.
- [ ] **Parent AC4 (restated in full):** Windows containing missing samples report the missing share as `unknown` (never as idle, never renormalised away); an integration/unit test drives a fixture sample stream with a deliberate gap and asserts the exact computing/idle/unknown split.
- [ ] **Parent AC5 (restated in full):** The CLI produces correct output with `proxy.log` absent — an integration test runs the query path against recorded Prometheus API payloads with no proxy log present, proving the figure is a direct measurement.
- [ ] **Parent AC6 (restated in full):** Unit tests cover window/step selection, threshold and percentage arithmetic (including boundary power exactly at 90 W), Prometheus response parsing/timestamp alignment, gap and partial-coverage handling, and sampler interval configurability; each test asserts observable behaviour rather than non-`None`.
- [ ] `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` reports, for an arbitrary window (`--since/--until` or `--window`, `--step`, `--prometheus-url` default `http://127.0.0.1:9090`), the computing-time percentage, idle percentage, unknown percentage, mean and max power in watts, and peak concurrent busy slots; `--json` emits the same figures machine-readably as a stable, documented schema.
- [ ] Windows containing missing samples report the missing share as `unknown` (never as idle, never renormalised away); a test drives a fixture sample stream with a deliberate gap and asserts the exact computing/idle/unknown split, and asserts the three shares sum to 100 %.
- [ ] The CLI produces correct output with `proxy.log` absent — an integration test runs the query path against recorded Prometheus API payloads with no proxy log present, proving the figure is a direct measurement.
- [ ] The output also shows the power-only fraction (`gpu:computing:bool`) so the two definitions can be compared, and `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation (the guard test covering this file passes).
- [ ] Unit tests cover window/step selection (including a step larger than the scrape interval and a window shorter than one step), threshold and percentage arithmetic including boundary power exactly at 90 W, Prometheus response parsing/timestamp alignment, gap and partial-coverage handling, and empty/all-unknown windows (explicit exit code and message); each test asserts observable behaviour rather than non-`None`.
- [ ] Invalid input is rejected with a clear non-zero exit: `--until` before `--since`, both `--window` and `--since/--until` given, unparseable duration, and a `--prometheus-url` that does not answer.
- [ ] The reported resolution states the step actually queried and the 15 s scrape floor, so the output never implies second-level fidelity.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_utilisation_cli.py` (new)
- `monitoring/tests/fixtures/prometheus_query_range.json` (recorded payloads from the test-first child)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` (reference only, no edits)

## Notes

Out of scope (parent constraint): feeding these figures into the daily usage
report's "Local model utilization" section — that stays a follow-up item.

## Goal

As an operator reading `monitoring/README.md` I can find the new slot series, run
the utilisation CLI from a copy-pasteable example, understand the retention and
resolution limits of the store, and re-measure the power calibration myself after
a hardware, driver or kernel change.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC7, AC8). The README already documents deployment,
the exposure boundary, the PromQL query cookbook and the "why not `amd-smi`"
evidence (LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL). This child adds the workload series, the CLI, the
retention/resolution statements and the calibration procedure, and closes the
documentation gap between the hardware figure (`gpu:computing:bool`) and the
usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`.

Two figures must not be conflated (see LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ, which measured a ~27
point divergence): the log-derived figure measures slot occupancy from proxy
events, the hardware+slot figure measures "GPU drew compute power while at least
one slot was busy". The docs must state what each answers and why neither
replaces the other.

## Minimal implementation

- `monitoring/README.md`: extend the "What runs here" table and the query
  cookbook with `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slot_busy`, `llama_slots_total`,
  `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and
  `gpu:computing_workload:bool`; add a CLI section with a real example run.
- New calibration subsection: idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W,
  and the re-measure recipe (`cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average`
  while idle and during a known-long generation; update the rule threshold and
  `server.llama_gpu_wedge_power_low_threshold_watts` together).
- Retention/resolution statement: 90 d, history starts when the TSDB was created
  (2026-10-25 19:22 on this host), observed resolution is the 15 s scrape interval
  even though the sysfs sampler writes at 10 s.
- Keep `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` accurate; update it only if the
  cadence/responsibilities actually change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC7 (restated in full):** Documentation is updated: `monitoring/README.md` gains the slot series, the CLI usage, the retention statement (90 d, and that history starts when the TSDB was created) and a calibration/re-measure section, plus an explicit note on how computing-time % differs from the usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`; code comments and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` stay accurate.
- [ ] **Parent AC8 (restated in full):** Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.
- [ ] Documentation is updated: `monitoring/README.md` gains the slot series, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI usage, the retention statement (90 d, and that history starts when the TSDB was created) and a calibration/re-measure section, plus an explicit note on how computing-time % differs from the usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`; code comments and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` stay accurate.
- [ ] The documented CLI example is copy-pasteable and its output block matches the real column layout produced by the sibling CLI child (verify by running it, not by transcribing an intention).
- [ ] The calibration section states the measured idle/computing bands and the re-measure procedure precisely enough that a clean host can reproduce the numbers, including which sysfs file and which config keys carry the threshold.
- [ ] `gpu_busy_percent` appears in the README only in the "not a utilisation signal" context; a grep assertion in the existing docs test suite (or a new assertion) enforces it.
- [ ] `monitoring/README.md` states the resolution floor (15 s scrape, 10 s sysfs write) and that the CLI reports the step it queried, so no figure implies finer fidelity than the store holds.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.
- [ ] Each of the parent's eight acceptance criteria is re-checked at completion against the shipped behaviour (a short pass/fail table in the completion comment links each criterion to the file or command that proves it), and any criterion the plan did not cover is raised as a comment on the parent instead of being quietly dropped.

This is the last slice: it documents what actually shipped, not the plan. If a
sibling child had to deviate (metric names, flag names, exit codes), the docs
follow the code and the deviation is recorded in the parent's plan changelog.

# Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests

## Goal

An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved full-suite command set
includes a command targeting `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, so a
future configuration or resolution change cannot silently re-blind the
dev-push gate (parent AC5).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** — repo full-suite gate never runs
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 unenforced tests).

**Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store, SorraAgents): upstream
`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands()` must emit an extra explicit-path pytest
command for project-local skill test directories. This child lands the guard
that would have caught the original gap; it must not start before the upstream
rule is installed, because the assertion is red until then.

## Minimal implementation

- New `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`; resolve the runner exactly like
  `.githooks/pre-push`: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first,
  then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- Import the resolved module with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and
  call `full_suite_commands(REPO_ROOT)` — no nested suite execution.
- Assert exactly one command whose pytest initial path targets
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`; assert the canonical repo command
  (`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`) is still present; assert
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `suiteCommands` key.
- Failure messages name SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` so a
  future reader knows what regressed and where the rule is documented.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`
- `.pi/test-config.json`
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Drift guard.** An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the
  resolved full-suite command set includes a command targeting
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, and it passes in the repo full
  suite (run via the test skill) once SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB's rule is installed.
- **AC2 — Additive, not a replacement.** The same test asserts the canonical
  repo pytest command is still present, so the skill command is proven
  additive.
- **AC3 — No-pin guard.** The test asserts `.pi/test-config.json` carries no
  `suiteCommands` key, with a failure message explaining that a pin would
  silently drop the skill tests and would also disable changed-scope
  selection.
- **AC4 — Resolver parity.** Runner resolution mirrors `.githooks/pre-push`
  (repo-local first, then the global install); the test imports `run_tests.py`
  through that resolved path and only calls `full_suite_commands()` — it never
  executes a nested suite and completes in well under a second.
- **AC5 — Explicit skip.** If neither runner exists the test skips with a
  reason naming the expected install path (documented limitation, D-P3), so a
  skip stays visible in the report rather than silently passing.


## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store) — the resolution rule this
  test asserts.
- No sibling dependency: this is the test-first item for the parent's
  enforcement work.

## Deliverables

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py` (new module, 3–5 tests).
data.title: Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests
